report.title: Sample review results
report.summary: Review terms matched to verified sources and items held for human review.
report.recordedModel: Sample rules matcher & citation checker · recorded
report.reviewScope: The sample contract states six 12-hour shifts per week. These results are not based on text you provided.

weeklyHours.title: Weekly working hours may exceed the limit
weeklyHours.clause: Six days a week, 12 hours per shift.
weeklyHours.explanation: This schedule totals 72 hours a week. The usual statutory limit is 48 hours; even with conditional overtime, weekly work must not exceed 60 hours.

dailyHours.title: 12-hour daily shift
dailyHours.explanation: The usual daily limit is eight hours, with work up to ten hours allowed subject to conditions. The stated 12-hour shift does not explain the basis for the remaining time.

unpaidOvertime.title: No additional overtime allowance
unpaidOvertime.clause: No separate allowance applies to additional hours.
unpaidOvertime.explanation: Section 108 sets the applicable overtime allowance at twice the ordinary rate. This clause says that allowance will not be paid.

uniformDeposit.title: Uniform cost deducted from wages
uniformDeposit.clause: A fixed amount for uniforms is deducted from wages each month.
uniformDeposit.explanation: Section 125 limits wage deductions to specified authorized grounds. This term gives no basis for an automatic monthly uniform deduction.

probationDuration.title: Nine-month probation period
probationDuration.clause: The first nine months after hiring count as a probation period.
probationDuration.explanation: The usual period is six months for clerical work and three months for other work; a skilled worker may receive a specific three-month extension. The basis for nine months is not stated.

terminationNotice.title: Employment may end without notice
terminationNotice.clause: The employer may end employment at any time without notice.
terminationNotice.explanation: For termination covered by section 26, written notice or wages in lieu apply according to worker category. This term states no limits or exceptions.

missingBreak.title: No break stated for a long shift
missingBreak.clause: No scheduled break is provided during a 12-hour shift.
missingBreak.explanation: Section 101 provides rest or meal breaks based on hours worked. A 12-hour shift with no break does not match that provision.

noWeeklyRest.title: Weekly rest day may be cancelled
noWeeklyRest.clause: Weekly rest may be cancelled when work requires it.
noWeeklyRest.explanation: Section 103 provides weekly holidays according to establishment type. An unrestricted cancellation term does not clearly preserve that entitlement.

missingAppointmentLetter.title: No separate appointment or identity card
missingAppointmentLetter.clause: These duty terms are final; no separate appointment letter or identity card will be provided.
missingAppointmentLetter.explanation: Section 5 says a worker may not be employed without an appointment letter and must receive a photo identity card. This clause directly denies both.

unconditionalUniformReplacement.title: Worker pays for every uniform replacement
unconditionalUniformReplacement.clause: The cost of a new uniform is deducted from wages when it wears out or is replaced.
unconditionalUniformReplacement.explanation: Wage deductions may only be made on grounds authorized by law. Section 125 does not authorize charging the worker the full cost of replacement for ordinary wear.

uncertain.title: 70% pay during probation
uncertain.clause: During the nine-month probation period, 70% of the basic wage will be paid.
uncertain.explanation: Applicable minimum wages can depend on industry, role, and wage structure. This sample does not provide enough information to assess the rate; no legal conclusion is given.

law.version: Text shown in the official law repository · Act No. 42 of 2006

section4.title: Worker categories and probation period
section4.text: The probation period for a worker employed in clerical work shall be six months and for other workers shall be three months: Provided that, in the case of a skilled worker, the probation period may be extended by a further three months if, for any reason, it is not possible to assess the quality of the worker’s work within the first three months.
section4.highlight: for other workers shall be three months

section5.title: Appointment letter and identity card
section5.text: No employer shall engage any worker without giving such worker an appointment letter, and every employed worker shall be given a photo identity card.
section5.highlight: without giving such worker an appointment letter

section26.title: Termination of employment by employer otherwise than dismissal
section26.text: For a permanent worker employed on a monthly basis, written notice of 120 days, and for any other permanent worker, written notice of 60 days may be given. Employment may be ended by paying wages in lieu of the notice period.

section100.title: Daily working hours
section100.text: An adult worker shall not ordinarily work, or be required to work, in an establishment for more than eight hours in any day: Provided that, subject to section 108, such worker may work up to ten hours in any day.
section100.highlight: for more than eight hours in any day

section101.title: Intervals for rest or meals
section101.text: A worker in an establishment shall not be required to work for more than six hours in any day unless the worker is given an interval of one hour for rest or meals on that day.
section101.highlight: an interval of one hour for rest or meals

section102.title: Weekly working hours
section102.text: An adult worker shall not ordinarily work, or be required to work, in an establishment for more than 48 hours in any week. Subject to section 108, total working hours must not exceed 60 hours in a week.
section102.highlight: more than 48 hours in any week

section103.title: Weekly holiday
section103.text: A worker in a factory or industry shall receive one day of holiday per week; a worker in a shop or establishment shall receive one and a half days per week.
section103.highlight: one day ... one and a half days per week

section108.title: Extra allowance for overtime work
section108.text: Where a worker works beyond the fixed hours under this Act, the worker is entitled to an allowance for overtime at twice the ordinary rate of basic wages, dearness allowance, and any ad hoc or interim wages, if any.

section125.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
section125.text: No deduction shall be made from the wages of a worker except those authorized by this Act. Deductions may only be made in accordance with this Act and within specified authorized categories.
section125.highlight: except those authorized by this Act

proposals.title: Suggested clause wording
proposals.description: These are discussion drafts, not final wording without legal review.

overtime.title: Overtime allowance
overtime.old: No separate allowance applies to additional hours.
overtime.new: For work beyond the limits set by law, overtime allowance will be paid in accordance with applicable law.

uniform.title: Uniform deductions
uniform.old: A fixed amount for uniforms is deducted from wages each month.
uniform.new: Any deduction from wages will be made only where authorized by law and after meeting the applicable conditions.

termination.title: Notice of termination
termination.old: The employer may end employment at any time without notice.
termination.new: Employment will end with written notice, or payment of wages in lieu, as required by applicable law.
